content: January 18, 2024 Español Types of Cancer What to know CDC provides basic information and statistics about some of the most common cancers in the United States. Types of Cancer Bladder Cancer Basics Smoking is the most important risk factor for bladder cancer. Dec. 6, 2023 Breast Cancer Talk to your doctor about when to start and how often to get a screening mammogram. Jan. 8, 2024 Cervical Cancer Screening tests and the HPV vaccine can help prevent cervical cancer. Jan. 10, 2024 Colorectal Cancer If you are 45 years old or older, get screened for colorectal cancer. Jan. 10, 2024 Gynecologic Cancers Learn about cancers that start in a woman’s reproductive organs. Jan. 15, 2024 Head and Neck Cancers Basics These cancers start in the head and throat, not including the brain or eyes. Oct. 24, 2023 Kidney Cancer Basics To lower your risk of kidney cancer, keep a healthy weight and don’t smoke. Nov. 6, 2023 Liver Cancer Basics You can lower your risk of getting liver cancer in several ways. Nov. 6, 2023 Lung Cancer Cigarette smoking is the number one cause of lung cancer. Jan. 15, 2024 Mesothelioma Basics Mesothelioma forms in the tissue that lines several internal organs. Nov. 6, 2023 Myeloma Basics Myeloma, also called multiple myeloma, is a cancer of the plasma cells. Nov. 3, 2023 Ovarian Cancer Learn about the symptoms and what you can do to reduce your risk. Jan. 15, 2024 Prostate Cancer Learn about the possible benefits and harms of screening and talk to your doctor. Jan. 17, 2024 Skin Cancer To lower your skin cancer risk, protect your skin from the sun and avoid tanning. Jan. 17, 2024 Uterine Cancer Several factors may increase the chance that you will get uterine cancer. Jan. 18, 2024 Vaginal and Vulvar Cancers Vaginal and vulvar cancers are rare, but all women are at risk for these cancers.
